stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Green cards, gutter balls, and grief
stories.text: On Monday, Popular Information revealed that Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, who President Trump nominated to permanently head the department, took multiple trips to China in 2015 as an attorney where he pitched Chinese nationals on investment projects in Florida. These events emphasized that investors would be eligible for green cards and would have access to “America’s Comprehensive Welfare.” Last year, Popular Information broke the news that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) stopped paying for third-party medical care for detainees on October 3, 2025. Eleven months later, ICE still has no system in place to pay for third-party medical care. Hospitals and other providers who have continued to treat detainees are owed millions of dollars. During this year’s Super Bowl, State Farm went all out for an ad riffing on Bon Jovi’s “Livin’ on a Prayer,” poking fun at rival insurance companies for only going “halfway there” with their coverage. This week, the ad was cited in a lawsuit brought against State Farm by Los Angeles County. The lawsuit alleges that State Farm failed to pay benefits to victims of the 2025 LA wildfires and seeks at least $160 million in restitution

stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Trump’s About To Let Wall Street “Pay To Play” With Your Pension
stories.text: The Trump administration just announced it intends to let Wall Street investment advisers pour campaign cash into the coffers of politicians who control access to trillions of dollars in workers’ retirement savings. President Donald Trump’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said Thursday that it plans to rescind its longstanding “pay-to-play” rule, which effectively bars investment advisers managing public pension money from donating to politicians overseeing where the money is invested. The development comes at a moment when Trump has opened the door to private equity and potentially cryptocurrency interests tapping Americans’ retirement savings. The “pay-to-play” rule was designed to ensure that decisions involving where public pension dollars are invested are made only with pensioners’ returns in mind, free from outside political influence. Photo: REUTERS/Feisal Omar MOGADISHU, Somalia — On September 3, shortly after sunset, U.S. surveillance drones began carrying out reconnaissance missions in two areas of the Al-Miskad mountains in Puntland, Somalia, according to Puntland security officials that spoke with Drop Site. The two localities—Togga Miraale and Togga Baalade—are considered strongholds for ISIS militants by local authorities. During the mission, the drones spotted alleged ISIS militants traveling with a donkey cart in the locality of Togga Baalade, the security officials said, and began carrying out airstrikes nearby at around 8:30 p.m. The strikes, which were accompanied by more drone surveillance missions that same day further northwest in the Sanaag region’s Al-Madow mountains where Al-Shabaab is active, broke a relative lull in U.S. attacks in Somalia. stories.title: The Thousand Martyrs Cup: Football Returns to Palestine After Three Years of Genocide
stories.text: An Ittihad Deir al-Balah football player jumps over an agility ladder in a training session ahead of the Thousand Martyrs Cup. August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah. On a dirt field in the dense coastal neighborhood of Deir al-Balah last week, players from Ittihad Deir al-Balah—one of Gaza’s three standing football clubs—gathered their torn balls, scuffed training cones, and rusted equipment. Surrounded by rubble and with Israeli drones buzzing overhead, they were preparing to train for a football tournament, the first in Palestine since 2023. Last month, the Palestinian Football Association (PFA) announced the return of football to clubs across Palestine and Lebanon after a three-year hiatus marked by Israel’s genocide in Gaza, terrorism in the occupied West Bank, and a brutal war on Lebanon. The resumption of the football association’s leagues in Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem, and Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon will open on September 4 with the Thousand Martyrs Cup, a two-month tournament named for the more than 1,000 Palestinian athletes killed by Israel since October 7, 2023. stories.author: Ken Klippenstein
stories.title: Nonbinary Gender Extremism?
stories.text: Sebastian Gorka Fundraising fell off a cliff this summer. Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. It isn’t for lack of material, which is a rare blend of both cry-laugh funny and substantively alarming. Gorka is like a theater kid version of Henry Kissinger, the same inflated ego but with a flair for the flamboyant: bragging he’s stacking terrorist corpses “like cordwood” after they’d received "eternal justice" from the Trump admin’s "hammers of hell”; his convertible with a vanity plate “ART WAR” (in reference to Sun Tzu); the Hercule Poirot pocket squares and mustachios; the Bond villain monologues delivered in a faint British accent. Amusing as it all is, the theatrics are in service of a worldview that regards just about anyone who looks or thinks differently from him as some kind of threat to Western civilization. You’d think he was auditioning to be the Oberführer of something that has nothing to do with America.
